title: game-brief
description: Structured intent for a bounded browser game prototype. Preserve mechanics, outcomes and assumptions independently of implementation choices.

title.description: Short working title for the prototype.

core_verb.description: Repeated player action or connected action sequence, including automatic actions that the player influences.

fantasy.description: Theme and setting retained throughout the build. The static-scene stage turns this intent into a complete scene; later stages add applicable behaviour and acceptance.

control_scheme.description: Discovery hint only; never mandates a controller or camera. Use custom when no hint fits. Run metadata records the actual implementation.

player_modality.description: Primary interaction: avatar (continuous or discrete actor), cursor (point/place/manipulate), menu (select/confirm), stationary (fixed viewpoint). Hybrids compose capabilities in run metadata; this label does not exclude other inputs.

fail_state.description: Loss condition, verifiable by a gameplay state machine within the time budget. Must be concrete (health reaches zero, timer expires, falls off the world), not vague.

win_state.description: Victory condition, verifiable by a gameplay state machine within the time budget. Must be a terminal state the loop can actually reach (defuse complete, lap finished, all waves cleared), not an open-ended goal.

interaction_tags.description: Semantic objects, actions or events used by the rules, including noncollision interactions. Empty is valid when no named tags are useful. IDs are unique within the brief.

id.description: Stable machine id, lowercase snake_case, unique within this brief.

meaning.description: What this tag represents in this specific game.

role.description: Semantic role such as hazard, resource, goal, action, information or another brief-specific role. Rules use IDs/events, not rendered colors.

time_budget_seconds.description: Simulation-time allowance for each purposeful validation scenario (30..300 seconds), separate from the wall-clock execution limit, not a mandatory game clock or idle timeout. Include all phases, including extraction after survival. Declare actual timer/turn rules in win_state, fail_state and context.

context.description: Structured carry-over for everything the fixed fields above do not capture, so a brief is self-sufficient without the original prompt. The object must be present; its properties are optional.

distilled_prompt.description: The distilled essence of the original prompt, including nuance and twists that did not map to the fixed fields. Downstream stages read this instead of the raw prompt.

twists.description: Unique mechanical twists the player must feel (e.g. 'kills rewind time', 'gravity flips on jump').

assumptions.description: What intake inferred and from what signal, so later stages can re-decide rather than treat inference as fact.

open_questions.description: Ambiguities left unresolved; later stages must resolve them or request input.

scene.description: Scene, board or interface intent. The first build stage renders all required thematic elements, including menu and board layouts; later stages make applicable behaviour and outcomes live.

description.description: Concise prose describing the play space, board or interface and required elements; no decorative quota or mandatory traversal. Record conflicting spatial requirements in context.open_questions.

theme_elements.description: Explicit thematic elements extracted from the prompt. Each element is rendered or represented in the static scene when applicable.

notes.description: Optional one-line distillation summary; anything richer belongs in context.

mode.description: Default polish; none only for an explicit omission of interface design. Acceptance still verifies outcomes, restart and delivery.

reason.description: The user requirement behind an opt-out.

style.description: Requested UI aesthetic, if any. Default theme uses dark teal panels, cream text and gold accents; no implied mechanics.
